claims.text: Processing-induced microstructural heterogeneity creates domains with differing thermal expansion coefficients.
Localized thermal-expansion mismatch creates internal residual stresses.
The internal residual stresses modify dislocation mobility.
The internal residual stresses modify elastic moduli and yield behavior.
Conventionally solidified, as-cast HfNbTaTiZr contains compositional and phase heterogeneities.
Homogenization can minimize phase segregation and compositional variation in HfNbTaTiZr.
Controlled aging or cold rolling can enhance microstructural segmentation in HfNbTaTiZr.
Solidification produces heterogeneous or segregated microstructures in this alloy system.
Cold work and aging produce heterogeneous microstructures relevant to thermal-expansion mismatch.
Residual stresses generated by heterogeneous thermal expansion alter creep rates.
Relative to a homogenized baseline, heterogeneous samples will have increased microhardness during cold rolling.
Relative to a homogenized baseline, heterogeneous samples will have a higher apparent work-hardening rate during cold rolling.
Heterogeneous samples will show a nonlinear and possibly stiffened temperature dependence of elastic modulus between 293 and 1100 K.
Heterogeneous samples will show altered tensile-creep rates at 1250 °C.
A homogenized sample will have lower internal thermal-stress fields than a heterogeneous sample.
The proposed comparison includes room-temperature cold rolling, elastic-modulus measurements from 293 to 1100 K, aging at 600–800 °C, and tensile creep at 1250 °C.
Solid-solution and precipitation hardening may overlap with effects attributed to residual stress.
The hypothesis would be falsified if heterogeneous and homogenized samples show no significant mechanical-response differences or if residual-stress fields do not correlate with those differences.
